summary: Defines a YANG data model for the topology of a data-center fabric, one possible view of how such a fabric is laid out. It covers the data model only and does not endorse any particular network design. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: A map format for the web of cables and switches inside a big computer room, so management software can read the layout in a standard way.

what is a yang data model for fabric topology
what is a data center fabric
what is a pod in data center networking
subtitle: A standard YANG model for describing a data-center network as a set of fabrics and the ports that join them.

tldr.problem: A data-center network can be made of several fabrics (PODs) built with different technologies, such as VXLAN and VLAN, and managing that mix is complex.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines YANG modules that extend the generic network topology model of RFC 8345 so that each fabric is a node, with attributes for its type, devices, links and ports, and with termination points standing for fabric ports.
tldr.outcome: A network controller can describe and expose its view of the fabrics it controls, and clients can work at the fabric level without knowing every underlay link and node. The RFC covers the data model only and endorses no particular network design.

today: RFC 8542 is a Proposed Standard, published in March 2019, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it. It builds on the network topology model in RFC 8345.

sections.title: Why Model Fabrics
sections.content:
A data-center network can be composed of one or more fabrics, also called Points Of Delivery (PODs). They can be heterogeneous. The RFC's example: Fabric A may use VXLAN while Fabric B uses VLAN, or a newer fabric may use a technique such as Geneve. Configuring and managing such a mix can be complicated.

The RFC treats a fabric as an atomic unit for management. Managing the data-center network then splits into managing each fabric separately plus managing the interconnections between fabrics. The document says this makes the overall task flexible and easy to extend.

The document focuses on the data model only. It does not endorse any kind of network design based on the model.
sections.eli5: A big computer room can have several separate zones built in different ways. It is easier to look after each zone on its own and then look after the connections between them.

sections.title: Terms and Model Layering
sections.content:
The RFC defines a POD as a module of network, compute, storage and application components that work together to deliver networking services. It represents a repeatable design pattern. A fabric is described as being composed of several PODs to form a data-center network.

The model sits in the family of topology models built on the generic network model and network topology model of RFC 8345. Alongside the Layer 1, Layer 2 and Layer 3 topology models, the fabric topology model is a further specialisation. It adds definitions specific to a data-center fabric, to give common configuration and operations for heterogeneous fabrics.
sections.eli5: A POD is like one repeatable building block of the computer room, and a fabric is made by putting blocks together. The fabric map is one more kind of map in a family of map types.

sections.title: A Fabric as a Node
sections.content:
The module ietf-dc-fabric-topology augments the generic ietf-network and ietf-network-topology modules. It does three things:

  • It adds a new network type to the network-types container, so a network can say it is a fabric topology.
  • It defines a fabric as a node, with a fabric-attributes container for things like gateway mode, fabric type, involved devices and links.
  • It augments termination points with a fport-attributes container. A termination point here stands for a fabric port that connects to an internal device, another fabric, or end hosts.

Because a fabric is just a node, clients can consume topology at the fabric level without knowing all the nodes and links of the underlay. A fabric topology can be configured by an administrator through the controller by adding devices and links, or it can be learned from the underlay network.
sections.eli5: On the map, a whole zone is drawn as a single dot, and the doors in and out of the zone are small connection points on that dot. You do not need to see every wire inside.

sections.title: Fabric Attributes and Options
sections.content:
The fabric-attributes container holds a fabric-id, a name, a type (the kind of underlay network, for example VLAN or TRILL), a description, and a vni-capacity container with a min and max VXLAN Network Identifier range. The identity list for fabric types includes VXLAN, VLAN and TRILL fabrics.

An options container carries:

  • gateway-mode: centralized (gateway on the SPINE node) or distributed (gateway on the LEAF node). The default is distributed.
  • traffic-behavior: normal (no policy needed for traffic) or policy-driven (traffic needs a policy, otherwise it is discarded). The default is normal.
  • capability-supported: a list of services, with the defined identities ip-mapping (NAT), acl-redirect and dynamic-route-exchange.

Three lists describe membership: device-nodes, device-links and device-ports. They refer to nodes, links and termination points that already exist in the underlay topology. Each device has a role list; the defined roles are spine, leaf and border, and the default is leaf. If more than two stages are used, users can define new role identities.
sections.eli5: Each zone has a name tag, a type, and some settings, such as where its main gate stands. It also keeps a list of which machines, wires and plugs belong to it.

sections.title: Fabric Ports
sections.content:
Each termination point gets a read-only fport-attributes container (config false). It has a name, a role, a type, a device-port and an optional tunnel-option choice for tunnels that connect two fabrics.

  • Role: internal (devices reaching each other inside the fabric), external (the fabric connecting to an outside network) or access (an endpoint connecting to the fabric).
  • Type: layer2interface, layer3interface, layer2Tunnel or layer3Tunnel.
  • Device port: a reference that maps the fabric port to a device node in the underlay.

The RFC states that termination point information is learned from the underlay networks, not configured by the fabric topology layer. For the member ports listed in device-ports, the port type is Ethernet or serial, and bandwidth identities include 1M, 10M, 100M, 1G, 10G, 25G, 40G, 100G and 400G.
sections.eli5: Each door of a zone is marked as an inside door, an outside door or a door for visitors. It also says whether it is a flat wire door or a tunnel, and which real plug it belongs to.

sections.title: Modules and Extension Points
sections.content:
The model is split into a types module (ietf-dc-fabric-types) with identities, typedefs and the fabric port grouping, and the topology module (ietf-dc-fabric-topology) with the augments. Many values are YANG identityrefs, so new device roles, port types, bandwidths and service capabilities can be added by defining new identities.

The model defines generic configuration and operational state which vendors can extend with vendor-specific information. The RFC leaves the way to compose a fabric, for example by an RPC, to vendor-specific implementation and does not provide it.

Appendix A adds a companion module, ietf-dc-fabric-topology-state, for implementations that do not support the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA). It mirrors the main module with non-configurable data nodes and augments ietf-network-state. Implementations that support NMDA SHOULD NOT support it.
sections.eli5: The map format has blank spots where makers can add their own kinds of machines, doors and speeds. There is also an older-style copy of the format for tools that cannot use the newer layout.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is meant to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF. Their mandatory-to-implement secure transports are Secure Shell (SSH) for NETCONF and TLS for RESTCONF. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) can restrict which users may use particular operations and content.

Two subtrees are called out. Writable data under fabric-attributes could be attacked by a malicious client trying to sabotage important attributes such as device nodes or type. Readable data under fport-attributes could be abused by a client trying to read the connections of fabrics without permission, such as device-port and name.

On the registry side, IANA is asked to register the namespace URIs and the YANG module names for the types, topology and topology-state modules.
sections.eli5: The map shows how the zones connect, so only trusted people should be able to read or change it. Locks on the doors and a guest list control who gets in.
